title: Compare prompt-level and hybrid feature surfaces for oracle-alpha predictiveness
description: resattn-7ve showed that coarse token-aware h_4[t] summaries help held-out alpha similarity a bit: position_thirds_mean_pooled_h_4[t]_resid_post_layer_3_concat beat the pooled baselines on pilot leave-one-out JS and modestly improved confirm R^2 and mean JS. But predicted routed loss stayed effectively neutral to slightly below uniform on average, so the Phase 1 held-out predictiveness blocker remains open. Next compare small prompt-level baselines and hybrid prompt-shape plus internal-state summaries on the pilot split only, then rerun confirm without changing the saved prompt registry.

title: Validate refusal-feature discovery workflow
description: Establish and validate the refusal-feature discovery path for the safety lane before making routing claims tied to refusal or honesty features.

title: Execute held-out alpha predictiveness check on development runner
description: Now that the development-model oracle-alpha runner and pilot stability suite exist, run the saved held-out predictiveness check from pilot to confirm on the development model, and either attach a concrete MIB-compatible sanity task or record a justified omission decision for this runner stage.

title: Test token-aware or prompt-level feature surfaces for oracle-alpha predictiveness
description: resattn-k2e compared a small pilot-only set of richer internal-state summaries for the development-model held-out predictiveness check. Mean-pooled h_4[t] was the best candidate, but confirm-split R^2 remained negative and predicted alpha performance stayed effectively at or slightly below uniform on average. Compare token-aware sequence summaries or prompt-level feature baselines on the pilot split only, then rerun the confirm check without changing the saved prompt registry.
close_reason: Completed token-aware oracle-alpha predictiveness comparison; logged follow-up resattn-27f for prompt-level and hybrid features.

title: Scale oracle-alpha runner to pilot batch with restart and perturbation checks
description: Expand the new development-model oracle-alpha runner beyond the two-prompt smoke. Run a larger pilot slice, execute the preregistered restart stability and prompt perturbation checks, and record whether the initial development-model improvements survive basic hardening.

title: Add identifiability, MIB, and predictiveness controls before claim-bearing oracle-alpha
description: Codify the Phase 1 control suite surfaced by the deep-research review. This includes: (1) a stability suite over optimization restarts and prompt resamples or paraphrases, (2) an out-of-sample alpha-predictiveness check on the confirmatory split, and (3) a MIB-aligned benchmark or sanity control when the task-model pair permits it. This should land before any claim-bearing interpretation beyond descriptive reconstruction.

title: Publish public prereg on LessWrong
close_reason: Dropped by explicit user decision; local prereg in history/PREREG.md remains the only mandatory prereg artifact.

title: Define and save pilot-confirmatory prompt split
description: Create and persist the pilot/confirmatory split before method tuning so claim-bearing results are not selected on the same prompts used for design.

title: Investigate stronger feature summaries for oracle-alpha held-out predictiveness
description: The first confirm-split predictiveness check in resattn-53q failed for the current sequence-level feature spec: mean-pooled h_1[t] on the development-model runner produced negative held-out R^2 and slightly worse-than-uniform predicted loss on average. Compare richer early-state summaries or alternative prompt-level features on the pilot split only, then rerun the confirm check without changing the existing pilot/confirm registry.

title: Wire oracle-alpha execution harness to saved Phase 1 control registry
description: Build the first oracle-alpha execution path on the development model and make it load the saved control registry by default. The goal is to exercise configs/oracle_alpha_controls_v1.yaml and the saved prompt registry on a small development-model slice, not to jump straight to claim-bearing scale.

title: Decide the Gemma-2 tuned-lens path and reproducible Figure 8 proxy
description: Resolve the two remaining implementation-shaping follow-ups from the deep-research review: (1) decide whether tool-breakage will train a custom Gemma-2 tuned lens or shift the tuned-lens comparison to a secondary model, and (2) define the reproducible proxy required for strong Figure 8 alignment claims, such as a small local AttnRes reproduction or another open depth-mixing comparison. Record the chosen path in DECISIONS.md before implementation reaches those lanes.

title: Freeze dependencies and start Phase 1 reconstruction checks
close_reason: Pinned the direct and transitive Phase 1 dependency set, installed the scientific stack into .venv with MPS available, and added the first reconstruction/cache-validity validation suite. Follow-up model-backed validation is tracked in resattn-ydp.

title: Add model-backed Phase 1 reconstruction and cache-validity checks
description: Extend the current validation module from toy linear-algebra checks to model-backed cache extraction and uniform-routing reconstruction on the development model. This should verify sublayer output accounting, final-normalization-aware reconstruction, and cache-validity identities on a real backend before broader oracle-alpha optimization.
close_reason: Added TransformerLens-backed model validation, including residual and logit reconstruction tests, a reusable smoke script, and a passing gpt2-xl MPS artifact for the configured development model.
